create.title: Exact near-product character-divisor kernel for M1
create.statement_tex: Let u_(L,H)(h)=v_L(h)Phi(h/(H+1))/h and K^+_(L,H)(z)=sum_(h>0)u_(L,H)(h)e(hz). With m_X(d)=floor(X/d+1/2) and n_X(d)=d m_X(d), the exact positive M1 block is its fixed constant times sum_n sum_(d:n_X(d)=n) chi_4(d)w_D(d)K^+((X-n)/d), equivalently d|n and -d/2<=X-n<d/2 with the specified tie convention. For real profiles, pairing positive and negative frequencies gives V_(L,H)(z)=(4/pi)sum_(h>0)u_(L,H)(h)sin(2pi h z) and the exact two-sided block sum_n C_(D,L)(n;X), where C retains the d-dependent V((X-n)/d). Exact products vanish because V(0)=0; one-sided exact-product and tie fibers are O_epsilon(X^epsilon). The weakest remaining lemma keeps the absolute value outside the entire (n,d)-sum and asks |sum_n C_(D,L)(n;X)|<<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon) on U_1.
create.next_action: Prove signed cancellation between distinct nearby products while retaining the odd kernel and its d-dependence.

create.title: Cross-product odd-kernel discrepancy estimate for the M1 residual corridor
create.statement_tex: For every (delta,ell) in the exact residual corridor U_1 and the actual fixed profiles, prove uniformly that |sum_n sum_(d:n_X(d)=n) chi_4(d)w_D(d)V_(L,H)((X-n)/d)| <<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon), where V is the exact paired odd Vaaler kernel, D=X^delta, L=X^ell, and n_X(d)=d floor(X/d+1/2). The proof must exploit cancellation between distinct nearby products or an equivalent ordered-denominator structure; separate absolute estimates for n-fibers cannot suffice.
create.next_action: Pair offsets across n=X or derive a signed operator estimate for the ordered denominator/product map. Preserve the actual profile and odd kernel.

create.title: Capacity obstruction to fiberwise or frozen-kernel closure of M1
create.statement_tex: On the critical window |X-n| asymp D/L in the M1 residual corridor, whole-shell replacement of the exact d-dependent kernel by an n-only coefficient has order-one error per divisor; target-sized absolute freezing requires at least H/L denominator cells and consumes the full desired saving. Moreover individual divisor fibers can be singleton or sign-locked. For fixed interior exponents, prime products n=dp with d,p=1 mod 4 and d in a nonvanishing actual-profile interval yield grouped l1 mass and squared l2 mass >> (D/L)/(log X)^2 for a suitable center X. Hence post-grouping triangle, coefficientwise, l1, l2, multiplicativity-only, complementary-divisor-only, and whole-shell frozen-kernel strategies cannot prove the residual target. This is not an obstruction to cancellation between distinct products in the total actual M1 sum.
create.next_action: Use this obstruction to reject any future proof that takes absolute values over product fibers before exploiting cross-product signs.

update.next_action: Prove the cross-product odd-kernel discrepancy estimate on U_1. Do not freeze to A_D(n), take fiberwise absolute values, or seek the missing power from divisor multiplicity alone.

reject.reason: At |X-n| asymp D/L, varying d across a dyadic shell changes the kernel by order one per representation; target-sized subdivision costs at least H/L cells.
Active divisor fibers can be singleton or contain only divisors with chi_4=+1; no uniform character-cancellation identity exists fiberwise.
Prime-product fibers with the actual nonvanishing profile have l1 mass and squared l2 mass >> (D/L)/(log X)^2 at suitable centers, exceeding the target by a power at fixed interior points.
The exact two-sided M1 kernel is odd and vanishes at zero; one-sided exact-product and tie fibers are divisor-bounded.

no_change.reason: The hard-top middle-frequency corridor remains a case of the open cross-product discrepancy estimate.
The final theorem remains conditional on open M9.

round_assessment.reason: Round 11 derives the exact signed near-product kernel and rigorously eliminates fiberwise, coefficient-norm, and frozen-kernel shortcuts, isolating cross-product odd-kernel cancellation as the first viable M1 residual lemma.
